about.title: Indio Car Accident Claims
about.longDescription: Indio's streets carry a mix of neighborhood traffic, commuters and travelers passing through on Rt 111. In 2025, public records show 201 injury collisions inside the city, with 266 people injured and 5 lives lost. Monroe Street, Indio Boulevard, Jackson Street and Rt 111 account for a large share of those reports, and crash counts tend to cluster on Tuesday afternoons between 2 and 4 p.m. Behind every one of those numbers is someone dealing with pain, missed work and phone calls from an insurer they didn't choose. We handle Riverside County car accident claims on contingency, so nothing comes out of your pocket unless there is a recovery. California gives you two years to file in most cases, but evidence fades far sooner. Photos, dashcam footage, witness contacts and medical records matter, and reaching out early helps protect them.

about.ctaText: Tell us what happened and we'll review your case for free.

items.title: Deadlines here are shorter than people expect
items.desc: California allows two years to file most car accident claims, but if a city, county or state vehicle was involved, a government claim may be due in as little as six months. We can pin down which clock applies to your crash.

items.title: Being partly at fault doesn't shut you out
items.desc: California uses pure comparative fault, meaning you can still pursue compensation even if you shared some blame; your recovery is simply reduced by your percentage. We push back when insurers overstate your share.

items.title: Your pain counts, and it isn't capped
items.desc: California places no cap on non-economic damages in ordinary car accident cases, so your pain, sleepless nights and lost routines are part of the claim. We work on contingency, so there's no fee unless you recover.

items.question: The other driver's insurance company keeps calling me. Should I give them a recorded statement?
items.answer: It's usually wise to politely decline until you've spoken with an attorney. Adjusters are trained to ask questions that can later be used to shrink or deny your claim, even when you're just being honest. You can share basic contact and policy information without agreeing to a recorded interview.

items.question: I was rear-ended on Indio Boulevard and the police report is still pending. Can I start a claim anyway?
items.answer: Yes. You don't need the final report in hand to begin, and waiting can cost you evidence like nearby camera footage or witness memories. Save your photos, keep every medical receipt, and note the businesses near the crash site. We can request the report from the responding agency and build the file while it's processed.

items.question: What does it cost to work with us?
items.answer: There is no upfront cost. Our team handles car accident claims on contingency, which means any attorney fee comes out of your recovery rather than your savings. If there's no recovery, you owe no attorney fee.
